introduction-automating-the-operator.core: Writing an operator means turning a human runbook into a reconcile function: given a custom resource, make the world match it, then report status. Good operators are idempotent, level-triggered, careful with errors and deletion, observable and safe to run concurrently with users and other controllers.

first_principles.problem: A homegrown operator works in demos but corrupts resources when retried or when objects are deleted.

analogy.title: Codifying a senior engineer's checklist
analogy.story: The checklist runs automatically, repeatedly and safely, whatever state things are in.
analogy.breaks: Engineers adapt to surprises; code must explicitly handle each failure mode.

example.title: Reconcile outline
flow: Ensure owned objects exist and match spec

the-toolkit-kubebuilder-and-operator-sdk.core: Kubebuilder scaffolds Go operators on controller-runtime: project layout, API types with markers (+kubebuilder:validation, +kubebuilder:rbac), controller stubs, webhooks, Makefile targets (manifests, generate, test, docker-build) and envtest. Operator SDK builds on Kubebuilder and adds OLM bundling, scorecard tests and Helm/Ansible operator types.

first_principles.problem: Engineers hand-write CRD YAML, RBAC rules and deep-copy code, introducing inconsistencies.
truths: Markers keep schema next to types.

analogy.title: A CAD tool that generates blueprints from your model
analogy.story: Change the model and every drawing updates consistently.
analogy.breaks: CAD drawings can be edited by hand; generated manifests should never be edited manually.

steps.label: Run
steps.detail: make manifests → CRD schema and RBAC regenerated.

check.q: What tool generates CRDs and RBAC from Kubebuilder markers?

project-structure-where-code-lives.core: A Kubebuilder project: api/v1/ (Go types for CRDs, generated deepcopy), internal/controller/ (reconcilers), cmd/main.go (manager setup: scheme, controllers, webhooks, metrics, health probes, leader election), config/ (kustomize manifests: crd, rbac, manager, webhook, samples) and test suites using envtest.

first_principles.problem: New contributors can't find where to change the API versus the controller logic.
truths: APIs and logic change for different reasons.

analogy.title: A well-organised kitchen
analogy.story: Recipes in one binder, cooking stations in another area, and the pantry layout documented.
analogy.breaks: Kitchens have one chef; operators may run multiple controllers in one manager.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Clear separation of API and logic.

check.q: Where is the controller manager wired up in a Kubebuilder project?

the-reconciliation-loop-the-core-engine.core: Reconcile(ctx, req) receives a namespaced name, not an event. It fetches the object from the informer cache, computes desired child objects, creates or updates them (CreateOrUpdate/Patch, server-side apply), sets owner references so changes re-trigger it, updates status and returns Result{RequeueAfter} or an error (which requeues with backoff).

first_principles.problem: A controller reacts to every child change by recreating children, causing churn and conflicts.

analogy.title: A gardener's daily rounds
analogy.story: Each round, check each plot against the plan and fix what's off, regardless of what happened overnight.
analogy.breaks: Gardeners walk every plot; controllers only reconcile keys that were enqueued or resynced.

check.q: What does Owns(&appsv1.StatefulSet{}) do in controller setup?
check.a: Watches StatefulSets owned by the custom resource and enqueues their owner when they change.

handling-not-found-errors.core: Reconcile requests can arrive after an object is deleted, so a Get may return NotFound. That's normal: return nil (client.IgnoreNotFound) since owner-reference garbage collection or finalizers handle cleanup. For children, NotFound means 'create it'. Treat other errors as transient and return them for requeue with backoff.

first_principles.problem: A controller logs errors and requeues forever for objects that were deleted.
truths: NotFound has different meanings for parent and child.

analogy.title: Arriving to service an appliance that's been removed
analogy.story: If the customer already threw it away, you just leave; if a part's missing, you install one.
analogy.breaks: Technicians call first; controllers simply re-check state each time.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Clean handling of deletes and missing children.

check.q: What should Reconcile return when the custom resource itself is not found?
check.a: No error (nil), because the object was deleted and there's nothing to reconcile.

idempotency-the-golden-rule.core: Because reconcile runs repeatedly, every action must be safe to repeat: create only if absent, update only differences, use deterministic names, avoid side effects that accumulate (duplicate cloud resources, repeated emails) and record progress in status or external IDs. Server-side apply and CreateOrUpdate help achieve this.

first_principles.problem: Each reconcile creates a new cloud bucket because names include timestamps.
truths: External systems may not be idempotent.

analogy.title: Pressing a lift button again
analogy.story: Pressing it twice doesn't call two lifts.
analogy.breaks: Lift buttons are built idempotent; your external API calls must be made idempotent.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: One bucket per database, however many reconciles.

check.q: Why avoid timestamps in names of resources an operator creates?
check.a: Each reconcile would generate a new name, creating duplicates instead of converging.

status-updates-communicating-with-users.core: Status reports observed state: conditions (type, status, reason, message, lastTransitionTime, observedGeneration), phase-like summaries and useful fields (endpoints, versions). Update via the status subresource, compare observedGeneration with metadata.generation so users know if the latest spec was processed, and emit Events for notable actions.

first_principles.problem: Users can't tell whether their change was applied or why a resource is stuck.
truths: Spec is intent; status is reality.

analogy.title: A parcel tracking page
analogy.story: It shows the latest stage, why it's delayed and when it last changed.
analogy.breaks: Tracking pages are read-only; status updates can conflict and must be retried.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: kubectl get db shows READY False with a reason.

check.a: Which version (generation) of the spec the controller last processed.

finalizers-handling-deletion.core: A finalizer is a string on an object's metadata that blocks deletion. When a user deletes it, Kubernetes sets deletionTimestamp but keeps the object until all finalizers are removed. Operators add their finalizer on create, perform external cleanup when deletionTimestamp is set (delete cloud resources, take a final backup), then remove the finalizer.

first_principles.problem: Deleting a Database CR removes Kubernetes objects but leaves an orphaned, billable cloud database.
truths: Owner references only clean up Kubernetes objects.

analogy.title: A checkout procedure before leaving a rented flat
analogy.story: You can't hand back the keys until the cleaning and meter readings are done.
analogy.breaks: Landlords chase you later; a stuck finalizer blocks deletion forever until removed.

check.q: What sets deletionTimestamp but keeps the object in etcd?
check.a: Deleting an object that still has finalizers.
